name: Independent on Sunday cryptic crossword No 1,428

clue.text: Leather overalls for men

blocks.note: first meaning: leather leg coverings worn over trousers by cowboys and riders
second meaning: informal word for fellows or blokes

explanation.surface: Someone describes protective leather workwear designed for male wearers.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads as one product description; split it after 'overalls' and 'for' simply joins the two meanings.
explanation.definitionFit: Cowboys wear leather leggings with that name, and the same word is casual British slang for blokes or fellows.

clue.text: What I've created here is an angry rumour

blocks.note: cross means annoyed
word as in 'the word is', a piece of gossip or news

explanation.surface: Someone apparently confesses that what they have produced is a furious bit of gossip.
explanation.walkthrough: The setter is speaking: what Gila has created here is the very puzzle you are solving.
explanation.definitionFit: The setter's own creation, the thing being solved on this page, is a grid puzzle of interlocking answers.

clue.text: Researcher's obsessive way assimilating something that's unknown

indicators.note: to assimilate is to absorb and take in, so one piece is swallowed by another

blocks.note: anal in the sense of fussily obsessive about detail
ST is the abbreviation for street, a way
algebra uses x, y and z for unknowns

explanation.surface: A scientist's compulsive method absorbs some mysterious element.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Researcher's' reads as a possessive, but the 's is 'is', joining definition to wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: An expert who examines data or samples closely in order to interpret them is a kind of investigator.

clue.text: Tight clothing hides middle of bum and 'bits'

indicators.note: only the central part of each following word is wanted, not its ends

blocks.note: hides as a noun: animal pelts
the central letter of the word bum
the two central letters of the word bits

explanation.surface: A clingy outfit conceals the wearer's rear and private parts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hides' looks like a verb, but it is the noun meaning animal pelts. 'middle of' applies to both bum and bits.
explanation.definitionFit: A close-fitting one-piece garment worn by cyclists, skaters and swimmers clings to the body like a second layer.

clue.text: Cops in California travel around with special toys?

indicators.note: travelling around means going back the other way, so the word for travel is read backwards

blocks.note: the Los Angeles Police Department
go means travel
S is a standard abbreviation for special

explanation.surface: Californian police officers travel about with unusual playthings.
explanation.walkthrough: 'toys' are toy dogs, the small breeds kept as pampered pets; the question mark flags that sense.
explanation.definitionFit: Small pampered pet breeds are called toy dogs, the kind that sit on an owner's knee.

clue.text: Grab stock from behind large, old boxes

indicators.note: to box something is to enclose it, so the outer letters wrap round the inner piece

blocks.note: L is the clothing-size abbreviation for large
a donkey is a farm animal, part of the stock, and the word is also slang for the behind
O is a standard abbreviation for old

explanation.surface: Someone seizes cattle from the rear of a large, ancient group.
explanation.walkthrough: The donkey is livestock, and its name doubles as a word for the rear, so 'stock from behind' points at one word two ways.
explanation.definitionFit: A cowboy's looped rope is thrown to catch a steer, and as a verb the word means to catch with it.

clue.text: The buttocks let out hot air

indicators.note: letting something out frees it, and freed letters are released into a new order

blocks.note: prat is old slang for the buttocks
taken as written

explanation.surface: A schoolboy joke about someone's backside breaking wind.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface is a fart joke; 'hot air' is really empty talk, and prat, before it meant a fool, meant the bottom.
explanation.definitionFit: Empty, foolish chatter that goes on and on is idle talk with no substance, just like hot air.

clue.text: Go round the M25? Not with a learner!

indicators.note: 'not with' means without, so the following letters are taken away from the motorway's name

blocks.note: the M25 is the London Orbital, the motorway ringing London
A as written plus L, the learner-driver plate letter

explanation.surface: A warning against taking a learner driver round London's busy ring motorway.
explanation.walkthrough: The M25 is the motorway that encircles London, known as the London Orbital. Drop A and L from its end.
explanation.definitionFit: A satellite or planet circles another body continuously, so the verb means to travel round in a loop.

clue.text: A legendary DJ's spinning some R.E.M.?

indicators.note: a DJ spins records, and spinning a word round turns it to face the other way

blocks.note: John Peel, the famous BBC Radio 1 disc jockey, plus the possessive S

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether a famous DJ is playing a record by the band R.E.M.
explanation.walkthrough: John Peel was a celebrated British radio DJ who championed new bands. R.E.M. is not the band but rapid eye movement.
explanation.definitionFit: Rapid eye movement is the dreaming phase of slumber, so a bit of it is a portion of night-time rest.

clue.text: Mineral revealed when a gas mine explodes

indicators.note: an explosion blows things apart, scattering the letters into a fresh arrangement

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A mining disaster: a gas explosion underground exposes a mineral deposit.
explanation.definitionFit: Magnesium oxide is a white compound found naturally and used in antacids, a chemical substance mined from rock.

clue.text: A world-class restaurant invents things, exceptional things

blocks.note: taken as written
Noma in Copenhagen, repeatedly named the world's best restaurant
to lie is to make things up

explanation.surface: A top restaurant creates remarkable new dishes.
explanation.walkthrough: Noma is a famous Copenhagen restaurant that topped the World's 50 Best list several times.
explanation.definitionFit: Oddities that depart from the normal rule or pattern are irregularities, cases outside the usual run.

clue.text: Proceed slowly and don't start to take risks

indicators.note: telling a word not to start means it loses its opening letter

blocks.note: to gamble is to take chances

explanation.surface: Advice to go carefully and avoid danger.
explanation.walkthrough: 'don't start to' reads as advice not to begin, but it means drop the first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: To walk at a leisurely, unhurried pace is to stroll along, moving forward without haste.

clue.text: Snooping is certainly not flipping positive

indicators.note: flipping something over turns it the other way round, so the word for positive is read backwards

blocks.note: an emphatic refusal
an affirmative answer

explanation.surface: Prying is definitely not a good thing, says someone with mild swearing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flipping' looks like a mild expletive in the surface, but it turns the word for positive round.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone prying into other people's business is inquisitive and meddlesome, poking about where unwelcome.

clue.text: Baseball player's pants and shirt?

blocks.note: short trousers
a top is an upper garment

explanation.surface: A question about what a baseball player's kit consists of.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's is 'is', not a possessive. In American English pants means trousers, so pants can be the short variety.
explanation.definitionFit: The fielder positioned between second and third base is a specific defensive role in baseball.

clue.text: He is too hammered to have the first bit of my drink

indicators.note: hammered means beaten out of shape, so the letters are knocked into a new order
only the very first piece of the following word is taken

blocks.note: taken as written
the opening letter of my

explanation.surface: Someone is too drunk to be given even a sip of my drink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hammered' means drunk in the surface, which suits 'drink'; here it tells you to rearrange the letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A thick blended beverage of fruit, yoghurt or milk is something you sip, a kind of beverage.

clue.text: Nuts put back a couple of times

indicators.note: putting something back returns it the way it came, so the doubled word is read backwards

blocks.note: to set is to put or place
the same word again, because a couple of times means twice

explanation.surface: Someone returned the nuts twice over.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a couple of times' says the reversed piece is written twice in a row.
explanation.definitionFit: Nuts is vulgar slang for the male reproductive glands, so the anatomical term is a fair equivalent.

clue.text: One shifted in a locomotive, transported only for a short time

indicators.note: a single letter is moved to a new spot within the string, a rearrangement of just one character

blocks.note: a locomotive pulls a train
to send is to dispatch or transport

explanation.surface: A passenger is moved within a train carriage and carried along only briefly.
explanation.walkthrough: Write TRAIN SENT and move just the one letter I of TRAIN two places along; nothing else changes.
explanation.definitionFit: Something passing and impermanent lasts briefly, so the adjective describes what exists only temporarily.

clue.text: Uncertainty shown by dodgy Trump acolyte on the radio

indicators.note: on the radio we only hear words, so the spelling can differ from what is said

blocks.note: sus is slang for dodgy, and Mike Pence was Donald Trump's vice-president

explanation.surface: Political doubt stirred up by a shady Trump loyalist's broadcast interview.
explanation.definitionFit: The anxious state of not knowing what will happen next is tension born of doubt or not knowing.

clue.text: Eminent old city said to provide housing

indicators.note: providing housing means giving a home, so one word lodges another inside it

blocks.note: to state is to say
Ur is the ancient Mesopotamian city

explanation.surface: A distinguished ancient city is reportedly going to provide homes.
explanation.walkthrough: Ur, the ancient Sumerian city, is the crossword's favourite old city.
explanation.definitionFit: Having stature or standing, a person of high reputation, is distinguished and prominent in public regard.

clue.text: Tesla gets involved in German car manufacturer's tests

indicators.note: getting involved in something means getting into it, so the unit goes inside the brand

blocks.note: Audi, the German carmaker, with the possessive S
T is the symbol for the tesla, the unit of magnetic flux density

explanation.surface: The electric carmaker Tesla joins in a rival German firm's trials.
explanation.walkthrough: Tesla is not the car company here but the SI unit, whose symbol is T.
explanation.definitionFit: Official inspections or examinations, especially of accounts or procedures, are checks or reviews.

clue.text: Bowl-like containers and pots often smeared with sauce

indicators.note: often suggests at regular intervals, so every other letter is kept
smearing spreads things about messily, so the letters lose their order

blocks.note: every other letter of pots, starting with the first
taken as written

explanation.surface: A kitchen scene of bowls and pans habitually smeared with sauce.
explanation.walkthrough: 'often' here means at regular intervals, so take alternate letters of pots.
explanation.definitionFit: Small round drinking vessels for a hot brew are shaped like little bowls with handles.

clue.text: Sci-fi film about small green animals

indicators.note: turning about means facing the other way, so the whole string is read backwards

blocks.note: S is the size abbreviation for small
green in the sense of inexperienced or unripe
rats are animals

explanation.surface: A science-fiction film featuring little green creatures, the classic aliens.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' looks like 'concerning', but it tells you to turn the whole string round.
explanation.definitionFit: George Lucas's 1977 space-opera saga is the most famous science-fiction movie franchise.

clue.text: Extremely risqué setter gets rejected and principally needs to straighten up some more

indicators.note: the extremes of a word are its two ends, so only those are kept
something rejected is sent back, so the setter's name is written backwards
principally means first and foremost, so the opening letter alone is taken

blocks.note: the first and last letters of risqué
Gila is the name of this puzzle's setter
the opening letter of needs

explanation.surface: A setter's naughty clue is turned down and must be tidied up further.
explanation.walkthrough: 'setter' is the compiler of this puzzle, here Gila, whose pseudonym is the piece to turn round.
explanation.definitionFit: To bring back into line, or straighten again after drifting, is to adjust the alignment once more.

clue.text: Fancy a drink immediately

blocks.note: to fancy is to like
a shot is a small measure of spirits

explanation.surface: An offer of a drink right now.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fancy a drink' sounds like an invitation; split it as a verb and a noun phrase.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means very quickly and without hesitation, as fast as a bullet from a gun.

clue.text: Zlatan's debut in the roster ... he scored

indicators.note: a debut is a first appearance, so only the name's opening letter is used
being in the roster means sitting inside it, so one piece goes within the other

blocks.note: a roster is a list of names
the opening letter of Zlatan

explanation.surface: Footballer Zlatan Ibrahimović makes his first appearance on the team sheet and duly scores.
explanation.walkthrough: 'scored' suggests a goal, but here it means wrote music: the answer is the Hungarian composer.
explanation.definitionFit: Franz, the Hungarian Romantic composer and piano virtuoso, wrote orchestral and piano scores.

clue.text: Jack Kerouac's novels are very entertaining at first

indicators.note: at first points to the beginning of each word, so the opening letters are strung together

blocks.note: the opening letters of these five words

explanation.surface: A literary verdict praising the Beat writer Jack Kerouac's fiction.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Jack' reads as Kerouac's first name, but it is the definition: the playing card.
explanation.definitionFit: In a pack of playing cards the jack is also called by an older name for a rogue or servant.

clue.text: He's a criminal protecting the heart of Cardiff underworld

indicators.note: criminal suggests something crooked or bent, so the letters are twisted out of order
protecting something means surrounding and shielding it, so the rearranged letters wrap round
the heart is the centre, so only the middle letter of the city is taken

blocks.note: taken as written
the central letter of Cardiff

explanation.surface: A gangster is shielding the centre of the Welsh capital's underworld.
explanation.walkthrough: 'underworld' fits the crime surface, but it means the Greek realm of the dead.
explanation.definitionFit: In Greek myth, the realm beneath the earth where souls of the dead dwell is named after its ruling god.

clue.text: Part of a supermarket is covered in beer

indicators.note: being covered in something means being wrapped by it, so the drink goes round the little word

blocks.note: ale is a type of beer
taken as written

explanation.surface: A section of a supermarket floor is soaked in spilt beer.
explanation.definitionFit: Shoppers walk along the passageways between rows of shelves in a store, each lined with goods.

clue.text: United supporters going round creating chaos

indicators.note: going round turns things to face the other way, so the combined letters are read backwards

blocks.note: U is the abbreviation for United in team names
fans are a team's supporters

explanation.surface: Football supporters of a United side run riot.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer is military slang, an acronym for 'situation normal, all fouled up'.
explanation.definitionFit: The military acronym describes a confused, botched situation, a muddle or total mess.

clue.text: Being filthy is ultimately pointless when playing around with Tinder

indicators.note: ultimately means in the end, so only the final letter of the next word counts
playing around means messing about, so the letters are jumbled into another order

blocks.note: taken as written
the final letter of pointless
taken as written

explanation.surface: A cynical verdict that dirty talk on a dating app gets you nowhere.
explanation.walkthrough: Tinder is the dating app, here just letters to rearrange; 'playing around' suits the dating surface.
explanation.definitionFit: The state or quality of being unclean or smutty is the abstract noun for grubbiness or crudeness.

clue.text: Performers missing out on the two leading parts in Hair?

indicators.text: missing out on the two leading
indicators.note: missing out on the leaders means losing the front two letters of the word

blocks.note: female performers on stage or screen

explanation.surface: Actors who miss out on the two lead roles in the musical Hair.
explanation.walkthrough: Hair is the 1960s rock musical, so 'parts' look like roles; they are really locks of hair.
explanation.definitionFit: Long locks of a person's head of hair are sections or strands of it, so they are its parts.

clue.text: Go mad, having binned your junk food

indicators.note: binning something throws it away, so the named word is removed from the phrase

blocks.note: do your nut is British slang for lose your temper
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone is told to get angry after their unhealthy snacks are thrown away.
explanation.walkthrough: 'do your nut' is British slang for flying into a rage; remove the word your from it.
explanation.definitionFit: A ring-shaped fried and sugared cake, spelt the American way, is a classic unhealthy snack.
